- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 86.03 → 86.79 or 85.30 → 86.76), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too much upward bias after peaks, fails to reflect downward drift.
- Forecast lags true trend by 1–3 days for downward moves; tends to predict downward turn too early or too late.
- High variance in forecast tails — especially last 5–10 days — often overpredicts volatility or misses sharp reversals.
- Model exhibits “sticky” bias: if history shows a downward trend, forecast remains above true mean for 3–5 days before adjusting.
- Avoids sharp downward corrections after high peaks — often underestimates the depth of the drop.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum — fails to account for macroeconomic or policy-induced reversals within 10 days.
- Tends to overfit recent spikes — model reacts too strongly to recent highs, underestimating subsequent pullback.
